messages:
nora: New hire blocked: unit tests fail in Vitest and Jest with errors from node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk dist/esm.
sam: What error text?
nora: `Unexpected token 'export'` and `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` depending on runner. Import is `import { createClient } from '@redwood-inference/sdk'`.
jamie: Classic ESM/CJS test-runner friction. Vitest can inline deps; Jest needs transformIgnorePatterns to include the package.
sam: For Vitest try: `deps: { inline: ['@redwood-inference/sdk'] }` + `resolve.alias` to a local CJS shim. That fixed it locally for me.
nora: We did that but CI uses Jest and still gets ERR_REQUIRE_ESM.
jamie: Jest tip: `transformIgnorePatterns: ["/node_modules/(?!@redwood-inference/sdk)"]` and enable ts-jest `useESM` if using ts-jest. Also sometimes set `NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules` on older Node in CI.
sam: Named export mocks in Jest are finicky. Use `jest.mock('@redwood-inference/sdk', () => ({ __esModule: true, createClient: jest.fn() }))` or use `jest.isolateModules` so module evaluation happens after mock.
nora: Thanks. Short-term we’ll keep the shim in the onboarding repo. Can SDK publish a small cjs build or a test-utils mock entry?
jamie: Good ask. I'll open an issue requesting: (1) dist/cjs build or cjs wrapper, (2) exports map covering common deep imports, (3) a `test-utils` export with createMockClient, and (4) examples for Jest & Vitest.
ci-bot: Issue #459 created: "js-sdk: test-runner ESM/CJS compatibility and mocking" assigned @jamie https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/459
nora: Perfect — will link the onboarding shim to the issue and update docs.
